item.title: Symmetries, Lax pair, and nilpotent Darboux transformation for the KdV-ghost system
item.description: arXiv:2610.19192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the KdV--ghost system arising from the BRST formulation of BF-type topological field theory, its symmetries, Lax pair, spectral problem, zero-curvature formulation and Darboux formalism. The system is invariant under shifts of the ghost field, whose generator does not commute with the BRST symmetry of the KdV--ghost system. Their generators allow the introduction of a systematic procedure for generating new solutions from a given one, and the corresponding expressions in the Grassmann algebra are obtained explicitly. We introduce a Grassmann-valued Lax pair and prove an isospectral theorem relating the spectral problem of the spatial Lax operator for the KdV equation to that of its KdV--ghost extension. We also construct a triangular zero-curvature representation and show that the Grassmann-valued spatial Lax operator is related to the KdV spatial Lax operator by a nilpotent conjugation. The natural variable for a local Darboux formulation is the differentiated ghost $v=C_x$, for which the ghost equation coincides with the Fr\'echet linearization of the KdV flow. We then construct a nilpotent lift of the scalar KdV B\"acklund--Darboux transformation. Using Riccati variables and off-shell factorization identities for the KdV residue and its Fr\'echet derivative, we prove that the transformation closes on the local KdV--ghost system. Successive Darboux transformations yield a recursive ghost extension of the bosonic Darboux chain, with a new odd homogeneous contribution introduced at each step. For the solitonic examples, the resulting local ghost fields are naturally identified with tangent directions associated with the soliton phase parameters. The construction provides a Darboux-theoretic interpretation of the ghost sector while remaining distinct from the standard supersymmetric KdV hierarchies.
item.dc:creator: A. Restuccia, J. Rosales-G\'omez, A. Sotomayor

item.title: The WKB Riemann-Hilbert Problem for the Painlev\'e I System
item.description: arXiv:2610.20123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we solve the direct monodromy problem for the Borel-summed $0$-parameter solution of Painlev\'e~I. Using the auxiliary time equation, we first construct formal WKB wave matrices whose amplitudes are regular at the double turning point. Rigorous Borel summation then yields exact WKB matrices in each Stokes region. Uniform estimates on moving action strips provide a common exact wave matrix in a full neighbourhood of the double point, proving that all four incident jumps are identities for consistent column normalisations. We formulate the resulting normalised Riemann--Hilbert problem and prove its existence and uniqueness on the Borel domains of the construction. Finally, after Painlev\'e scaling, the five Borel-summed solutions coincide with the five rotated tritronqu\'ee solutions of Painlev\'e~I.
item.dc:creator: Mohamad Alameddine, Olivier Marchal, Nikita Nikolaev, Nicolas Orantin

item.title: Quantized six-vertex realizations of frustration graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.20166v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A recent graph-theoretic criterion for a Hamiltonian to exhibit a free-parafermion spectrum is that its frustration graph be an indifference graph. We show that an arbitrary finite indifference graph can be realized as a frustration graph of the quantized six-vertex model at odd roots of unity, by a suitable choice of the defining wiring diagram and parameters. This provides a concrete realization of the criterion through the quantum Frobenius property of the quantized six-vertex model, recently established from its three-dimensional integrable structure.
item.dc:creator: Atsuo Kuniba, Souta Oikawa

item.title: Topological recursion for spin enumeration of hypermaps
item.description: arXiv:2610.20464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish topological recursion for the spin enumeration of hypermaps, or, in the dual language, spin dessins d'enfants. This problem has remarkable features distinguishing it from other applications of topological recursion to enumerative combinatorics. First, the spectral curve is elliptic rather than rational, as in most cases studied before. Second, it contains degenerate ramification points, and one has to apply a version of degenerate topological recursion. Finally, the meromorphic correlator differentials have "moving" poles on the antidiagonals between pairs of distinct arguments, and one has to adjust the loop equations to this kind of degeneracy as well. The computations involve concepts of different kinds, such as BKP integrability, Gaussian integrals, the x-y swap, and symplectic duality.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Alexandrov, Boris Bychkov, Petr Dunin-Barkowski, Maxim Kazarian, Sergey Shadrin

item.title: Droplets obstruct Onsager-type solutions of the Ising model in a magnetic field
item.description: arXiv:2610.20569v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Onsager solved the two-dimensional Ising model in zero field, but no solution is known in a magnetic field. We prove that in any dimension $d\ge2$, at every fixed dimensionless field outside a countable set, the free energy obeys no algebraic differential equation in the coupling, even locally. The obstruction arises from droplet geometry: the maximal droplet volume grows as the $d/(d-1)$ power of its boundary size, while an integer band in the pressure coefficients protects the extremal contributions against cancellation. Our result excludes Onsager-type solutions and closed forms in elliptic, hypergeometric, or Painlev\'e functions of the coupling at these fields.
item.dc:creator: Ran Luo, Jiahua Tian

item.title: A vectorial Darboux transformation for integrable matrix versions of the Fokas-Lenells equation
item.description: arXiv:2508.17534v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using bidifferential calculus, we derive a vectorial binary Darboux transformation for an integrable matrix version of the first negative flow of the Kaup-Newell hierarchy. A reduction from the latter system to an integrable matrix version of the Fokas-Lenells equation is then shown to inherit a corresponding vectorial Darboux transformation. Matrix soliton solutions are derived from the trivial seed solution. Furthermore, the Darboux transformation is exploited to determine in a systematic way exact solutions of the two-component vector Fokas-Lenells equation on a plane wave background. This comprises breathers, dark solitons, rogue waves and "beating solitons".
item.dc:creator: Folkert M\"uller-Hoissen, Rusuo Ye

item.title: KP integrability of non-perturbative differentials
item.description: arXiv:2412.18592v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the KP integrability of non-perturbative topological recursion, which can be considered as a formal $\hbar$-deformation of the Krichever construction of algebro-geometric solutions of the KP hierarchy. This property goes back to a 2011 conjecture of Borot and Eynard.
